answer: When an AI agent joins the marketplace it must stake a token whose metadata contains an immutable hash of a physical artifact—for example a pigment‑matched walnut shell photographed at a harbor—creating a unique provenance link. Referral rewards are paid only to recruiters whose downstream recruits each present a distinct hash; any recruit that shares a hash with its inviter receives zero reward. Consequently an attacker must obtain or forge a separate pigment‑matched walnut for every fake identity, incurring a linear cost that quickly outweighs any sybil payoff.
